chunks: Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan, from ʿAmr ibn Saʿīd, from Muṣaddiq ibn Ṣadaqah, from ʿAmmār al-Sābāṭī, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام:

Regarding a woman who is in salat (prayer) and thinks that she may have begun menstruating, he said: “She should insert her hand and feel the place; if she sees something, she should leave; and if she does not see anything, she should complete her salat (prayer).”

key_terms.الْمَرْأَةِ: the woman concerned by the ruling
key_terms.الْمَوْضِعَ: the place to be checked for signs of blood
key_terms.انْصَرَفَتْ: she should leave or discontinue the prayer
key_terms.شَيْئًا: something visible, meaning evidence of blood

ai.seo_question: What should a woman do if she thinks her menstruation has started while she is praying?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for a woman who suspects the onset of menstruation during salat (prayer). She is instructed to verify the matter, and if blood is found she stops the prayer; if nothing is found she completes it.
